use_case_solved: Detect broken container event sequences — a box that gated in and never gated out, a Let Export Order with no subsequent move, a scan selection with no scan — and raise WARN/CRIT findings the notifications service fans out.
training_data_source: None. This is a deterministic rule engine; it has no fitted parameters. The n=400 labelled synthetic set is used to MEASURE it, not to train it.
objective_function: Not applicable — no optimisation. The rules encode operational SLAs (72 h gate-out, 48 h post-LEO move, 24 h scan start), which an operations manager can check by hand.
model_used: Deterministic rule engine, 3 rules over the ordered event trail.
rationale: A rule an operations manager can read and challenge is worth more here than a learned model, because the corpus carries no labelled anomaly outcomes to fit against. Precision on a rule set is also a stronger claim than precision on a fitted model: it holds by construction rather than by sampling.
link_to_model_weights: models/uc2/event-anomaly-detector/rules.json — THERE ARE NO WEIGHTS. The rule set is the artefact; see its `why_not_model_weights` field.

validation_data.headline: Labelled synthetic set, n=400, seed 505
validation_data.real_world: Run over the corpus the detector produces 1,139 findings across 1,136 of 1,401 containers (see UC2-018). Those findings are unlabelled — the corpus states no ground truth for them — so they demonstrate coverage, not precision.

metrics.coverage_caveat: Measured on rule 1 (ANOMALY_MISSING_GATE_OUT) only. Rules 2 and 3 are not exercised by the labelled set.

known_overstatements_corrected_here: The service reports its algorithm as a 'rule engine + IsolationForest hybrid'. The IsolationForest is trained at import and never consulted — no output depends on it. Corrected to 'deterministic rule engine'.
Precision 1.0 is quoted without coverage. It measures one of three rules, against a negative case that cannot produce a false positive by construction. Stated in full here.
